title: Parameterized SQL from Node.js
summary: Use prepared statements and parameters so API input becomes safe database queries instead of string-built SQL.

sketchBlocks.cardTitle: Keep values out of SQL text
sketchBlocks.title: Prepared statements separate SQL structure from client-supplied values
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
When a request value becomes part of a query, keep the SQL text fixed and bind the value separately.

```js
const findByCategory = db.prepare(`
  SELECT id, title, category
  FROM events
  WHERE category = ?
  ORDER BY id
`);

const rows = findByCategory.all(category);
```

**Line by line:** `db.prepare(...)` creates a reusable statement. The `?` placeholder marks a value position without embedding the value into the SQL string. `.all(category)` binds the JavaScript value when the query runs and returns all matching rows. The row columns line up with the API's JSON resource fields.

Do not build SQL such as `"... WHERE category = '" + category + "'"`. Keep client values separate from SQL structure.

sketchBlocks.cardTitle: Write values safely and read the stored row
sketchBlocks.title: INSERT parameters create durable rows without string-building SQL
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
INSERT statements should bind values the same way SELECT statements do.

```js
const insertEvent = db.prepare(`
  INSERT INTO events (title, category)
  VALUES (?, ?)
`);

const result = insertEvent.run(title, category);
const created = findById.get(Number(result.lastInsertRowid));
```

**Step by step:** the SQL declares the columns and two placeholders. `.run(title, category)` binds the values and performs the insert. SQLite reports the generated row id. A parameterized lookup then reads the stored row back so the API can return the database representation rather than a guessed object.

The same placeholder rule applies to UPDATE and DELETE values as the persistence layer grows.

tryItExercises.title: Insert and read back a club
tryItExercises.prompt: Prepare an INSERT into `clubs(name, focus)` using placeholders. Run it with `Design Circle` and `design`, then use the generated id in a parameterized SELECT to read the created club.
tryItExercises.hint: Bind both INSERT values and the generated id through statement parameters.

help.concept: Parameterized writes keep request values out of SQL text and let the application read back the actual stored row.
help.hint_1: The INSERT needs one placeholder per inserted column.
help.hint_2: Use the generated row id as the bound value in a second prepared statement.
